title: Compare Options Against the Same Criteria
status: New proposed Lesson 04 production script, 2026-10-29. No new animation or narration in this handoff.
learningOutcome: Compare two concrete proposals using the same task-relevant criteria, while separating possible advantages from unverified outcomes.

scenario.task: Plan how a group will use an answer-help tool during a twenty-minute practice session with two sample problems. The aim is to understand the key reasoning, not merely finish answers.
conditions: The fictional tool can offer a hint or a worked answer
Tool output is not independently verified
scenario.baselineQuote: An answer tool can save time when we get stuck. I would use it as soon as a problem becomes difficult.
scenario.scope: No institution, official test, observed learner performance or measured outcome is represented. S07 transfers to a new event-notice layout discussion. The baseline quote does not specify whether the help is a hint or a full answer.

blocks.title: Give Both Options the Same Questions
Check the Reasoning Behind a Preference
Make a Comparison the Group Can Use

L04.S04.c001.speaker: coach
L04.S04.c001.text: A disagreement becomes easier to examine when the alternatives are clear. Instead of defending a preferred option against a vague problem, ask what each proposal would involve. Then compare both against the same questions.
L04.S04.c001.visualEn: Begin on a formal board with two empty proposal spaces and a shared criteria rail. Keep characters offstage.
L04.S04.c001.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L04.S04.c001.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L04.S04.c002.speaker: coach
L04.S04.c002.text: Our fictional group is planning a twenty-minute practice session with two sample problems. The aim is to understand the key reasoning, not simply finish more answers. The tool can offer a hint or a full worked answer. Neither kind of output has been verified.
L04.S04.c002.visualEn: Restore the fixed task facts; use a single undivided twenty-minute boundary, never invented minute allocations. Mark both tool outputs unverified.
L04.S04.c002.anchorHint: Neither kind of output has been verified
L04.S04.c002.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L04.S04.c002.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L04.S04.d001.speaker: maya
L04.S04.d001.text: An answer tool can save time when we get stuck. I would use it as soon as a problem becomes difficult.
L04.S04.d001.visualEn: Use a brief exact-quote appearance from Maya. Do not display a completed session or an adopted plan.
L04.S04.d001.anchorHint: as soon as a problem becomes difficult
L04.S04.d001.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L04.S04.d001.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L04.S04.c003.speaker: coach
L04.S04.c003.text: Return to Maya’s original wording, before the clarification explored earlier. It leaves the kind of help open. For comparison, take one possible version: open a full worked answer immediately. Set it beside another proposal: make a brief attempt, then request a focused hint if needed.
L04.S04.c003.visualEn: Explicitly restore the original statement before the separate earlier clarification. Keep an Original statement label on its card. Reveal full-answer-immediately as One possible version, not the only meaning of Maya’s words, then a separate brief-attempt-and-hint option. Reset prior illustrative decisions, outcomes and mode assumptions; neither candidate is adopted.
L04.S04.c003.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L04.S04.c003.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L04.S04.c004.speaker: coach
L04.S04.c004.text: Use four questions here: how would time be used, what reasoning would participants examine, could someone get started, and how would the group check the tool’s output? These come from this task. They are not a universal scoring system.
L04.S04.c004.visualEn: Reveal four shared row headings once. Both proposal columns use these exact headings; no points, weights, stars or green winner column.
L04.S04.c004.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L04.S04.c004.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L04.S04.c005.speaker: coach
L04.S04.c005.text: A worked answer could provide an entry point or a sequence to examine. It also takes time to read and check. Seeing a complete solution does not show that each person understands why its steps follow. Those possibilities belong in the comparison together.
L04.S04.c005.visualEn: Inspect only the full-answer column. Use conditional possibility cards and an unanswered understanding question. Never show measured time saved or observed comprehension.
L04.S04.c005.anchorHint: does not show that each person understands
L04.S04.c005.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L04.S04.c005.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L04.S04.c006.speaker: coach
L04.S04.c006.text: A brief attempt could help someone identify a particular gap before asking for a hint. But an attempt without a starting point can use time without clarifying much. The hint may help, or it may be unclear or inaccurate. It still needs checking.
L04.S04.c006.visualEn: Inspect the attempt-and-hint column under the same rows. Keep inability to start as a legitimate condition, without blaming the learner or drawing guaranteed improvement.
L04.S04.c006.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L04.S04.c006.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L04.S04.d002.speaker: learner
L04.S04.d002.text: I would prefer a brief attempt before a hint, because it might show us which step needs help. How would we support someone who cannot find a first step?
L04.S04.d002.visualEn: Brief authored reply. Connect the preference to a possible mechanism and retain its question. Use a dashed link rather than a proof arrow.
L04.S04.d002.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L04.S04.d002.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L04.S04.c007.speaker: coach
L04.S04.c007.text: This reply explains a preference and names a limit. It does not prove that the proposal is faster. Check whether your comparison gives both options the same chance: do not count checking time for one while pretending the other needs none.
L04.S04.c007.visualEn: Return to the criteria board. Align the two checking-time entries and keep all empirical outcomes unknown.
L04.S04.c007.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L04.S04.c007.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L04.S04.c008.speaker: coach
L04.S04.c008.text: Checking could include testing a suggested step against the problem’s conditions and asking why it follows. If the group cannot verify it, keep that uncertainty visible. A fluent explanation from the tool is not, by itself, confirmation.
L04.S04.c008.visualEn: Use a short verification pathway: proposed step, problem conditions, reason for the step, unresolved uncertainty if needed. Do not invent access to an expert or an answer key.
L04.S04.c008.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L04.S04.c008.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L04.S04.c009.speaker: coach
L04.S04.c009.text: Choose one criterion and compare both proposals privately. Include a possible benefit or limit for each. You can pause for more time. The aim is a fair comparison, not finding the sentence that makes your preferred option win.
L04.S04.c009.visualEn: Leave a blank private comparison space beneath the two proposal cards. Hide the upcoming example; do not populate the learner’s response.
L04.S04.c009.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L04.S04.c009.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L04.S04.d003.speaker: learner
L04.S04.d003.text: A full answer might help us start, but we would still need to check its reasoning. An attempt might reveal a gap, but someone could need help before making progress.
L04.S04.d003.visualEn: Show a separate One possible comparison card. Its two clauses refer to possible effects, not measured results.
L04.S04.d003.anchorHint: still need to check its reasoning
L04.S04.d003.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L04.S04.d003.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L04.S04.c010.speaker: coach
L04.S04.c010.text: No winner has been proved. The comparison identifies something the proposal must handle: getting started without losing attention to reasoning. Next, we will revise a suggestion around that concern while keeping agreement and open questions distinct.
L04.S04.c010.visualEn: Settle on the unresolved starting-help question. Keep the group decision and session outcome explicitly open.
L04.S04.c010.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L04.S04.c010.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L04.S04.h101.purpose: Privately notice a question that needs to be applied to both options.
L04.S04.h101.visualEn: Keep the four shared criteria and both proposal names readable. No automatic selection or claimed learner answer.

L04.S04.h102.purpose: Form a private comparison before hearing one example.
L04.S04.h102.visualEn: Keep the private response area blank and the same criterion headings available.

boundary: Use formal explanation and short examples. No perpetual three-person scene; no school, exam, policy or assessed-learner claim.
